key_insight: The paper introduces the first high-order finite element method that remains accurate for perfect conductivity and linear elasticity problems with nearly touching inclusions, even as gradients blow up.
engineering_relevance: This enables reliable simulation of stress and electric-field concentration in composite materials and microstructures where small gaps between rigid/perfect inclusions control failure or performance.
method: Derive asymptotic estimates for high-order solution derivatives near nearly touching inclusions.
Use a graded mesh to resolve narrow gap regions efficiently.
Construct auxiliary basis functions from the derivative estimates to support high-order FEM accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 2D and 3D numerical examples showing the expected convergence rates and demonstrating gradient blow-up as the inclusion gap shrinks.
watch_item: Performance and implementation may be sensitive to mesh grading and auxiliary basis construction, especially in complex 3D geometries.
paper_title: High-order finite element method for perfect conductivity and linear elasticity with nearly touching inclusions
